A '''quasimartingale''' is a concept from [[stochastic processes]] and refers to a [[stochastic process]] that has finite [[Expected value|mean]] [[Total variation|variation]]. Quasimartingales are generalizing [[semimartingales]] in the sense as they do not have to be [[Càdlàg function|càdlàg]], and they are exactly semimartingales if they are càdlàg. Quasimartingales were introduced by the American mathematician [[Donald Fisk]] in 1965.<ref>{{Cite journal | author = Donald L. Fisk | title = Quasi-martingales | journal = Transactions of the American Mathematical Society | year = 1965 | volume = 120 | issue = 3 | pages = 369–389 | doi = 10.1090/S0002-9947-1965-0192542-5 | url = https://www.ams.org/tran/1965-120-03/S0002-9947-1965-0192542-5| url-access = subscription }}</ref>

Some authors use the term as a synonym for semimartingale and assume the process is càdlàg.

== Quasimartingale == 
Let <math>(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, (\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \geq 0}, P)</math> be a [[Filtration (probability theory)|filtred]] [[probability space]] and let <math>\tau</math> be a [[partition of an interval|partition]] of the interval <math>[0, \infty]</math>. Further, let <math>X = (X_t){t \geq 0}</math> be an [[adapted process|adapted]] stochastic process. The ''(mean) variation of <math>X</math>'' is defined as
:<math>\operatorname{Var}(X) := \sup\limits_{\tau} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum\limits_{i=0}^n \left|\mathbb{E}[X_{t_i} - X_{t_{i+1}} | \mathcal{F}_{t_i}]\right|\right]</math>

The process <math>X</math> is a '''quasimartingale''' if <math>\mathbb{E}[|X_t|] < \infty</math> for all <math>t</math> and the process has finite variation:
:<math>\operatorname{Var}(X) < \infty.</math><ref>{{Cite book | author = Philip E. Protter | editor = Springer | title = Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations | year = 2004 | isbn = 3-540-00313-4 | pages = 116}}</ref>

=== Properties ===
*Every semimartingale is a quasimartingale.
*A quasimartingale is a semimartingale if and only if it is [[Càdlàg function|càdlàg]].<ref>{{Cite book | author = Philip E. Protter | editor = Springer | title = Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations | year = 2004 | isbn = 3-540-00313-4 | pages = 127}}</ref>
* [[Rao's theorem]] is formulated for quasimartingales.
